idiom_name: Codable conformance synthesised by the compiler (JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder), with the schema artifact published alongside
implementation_notes: Swift absorbs the binding layer: conforming a struct to Codable makes the compiler synthesise init(from:) and encode(to:), JSONDecoder/JSONEncoder own the wire form, and a CodingKeys enum (or keyDecodingStrategy) maps property names to the published ones. The contract artifact itself stays external - a JSON Schema/OpenAPI document, or protobuf through swift-protobuf - because the language only knows the shape of the Swift type; publish it from CI and diff it like any other interface. The hand-written custom init(from:) remains the right tool when the wire shape differs from the model or a field must be validated during decoding.
pitfalls: Synthesised Codable fails on the first missing non-optional key: additive evolution relies on optionals or a custom init(from:) using decodeIfPresent, otherwise a producer-side addition or removal breaks decoding.
A String-backed enum without a case for an unknown raw value throws at decode time; published code lists evolve, so handle unknown values explicitly instead of crashing the decode.
JSONDecoder is strict about ranges (UInt64 beyond Int64, Decimal) and throws: validate the schema at the seam so a producer bug is not reported as a consumer decoding failure.
